value.body: The Central Public Works Department and state public works departments employ architects to design and oversee government buildings — offices, hospitals, housing, campuses and heritage works. Central Group A architect posts in CPWD are filled through UPSC recruitment advertisements; state PWD posts through state PSCs or state recruitment boards.

items.label: Central recruitment
items.note: Usually shortlisting and interview; some posts have a recruitment test

items.label: State recruitment
items.note: Post names and rules vary by state

items.label: UPSC Assistant Architect (CPWD) vacancies
items.note: Degree in Architecture plus Council of Architecture registration required

items.label: Earlier UPSC CPWD Assistant Architect recruitment

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Arch and registration with the Council of Architecture. Watch UPSC's recruitment advertisements for CPWD architect posts and your state PSC's notices for PWD posts; some posts ask for prior experience under a registered architect.

value.title: At a glance
items: Openings are irregular and few compared with the number of B.Arch graduates.
Work leans towards public buildings, standards and project coordination rather than independent design.
Other public employers of architects include development authorities and municipal bodies.

value.title: B.Arch enrolment
value.note: All years of the five-year course combined; this is the pool of architecture graduates, not PWD posts.
value.source: AISHE reports 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24 (Ministry of Education), programme-wise enrolment table — B.Arch, all modes
